incident_spec.summary: Investigating the performance and concurrency behavior of large transactions in PostgreSQL, focusing on row locking, read/write interactions, and transaction conflicts.
symptoms: Blocked transactions due to row-level locks
Potential deadlocks or serialization errors in concurrent transactions
incident_spec.mechanism: PostgreSQL's MVCC (Multiversion Concurrency Control) and transaction isolation levels determine how rows are locked and accessed during transactions.

value.description: Reads do not block writes, and writes do not block reads.
Higher isolation levels may lead to serialization errors or blocking.
Concurrent transactions attempting to update the same rows are blocked until the first transaction commits.

assumptions: The database schema and workload involve multi-million row tables with indexed columns.
The transaction updates approximately 50k rows in a single operation.
unknowns: Exact schema details and workload distribution
Impact of specific isolation levels on performance and concurrency
